|lore=275 gunners manning 60 turbolaser batteries provide a wide firing arc. Even so, asteroids are a challenge due to the sluggish recharge rates of the high-powered blasters.
|game_text=If opponent just initiated battle, you may immediately fire one non-lightsaber, non-permanent weapon present in that battle (for free), adding 2 to each of its destiny draws. That weapon may fire again this battle.

|notes=The Players Committee released the original-layout slip for Defensive Fire on 30 May 2003. The published Set 5 editions are linked as [[Defensive Fire (V) (Virtual Set 5: A Dark Time)|Original]], [[Defensive Fire (V) (Virtual Set 5: A Dark Time) (Errata)|Revised (June 2003)]], and [[Defensive Fire (V) (Virtual Set 5: A Dark Time) (Errata 2)|Remastered (2006)]]. The first sheet was released 30 May 2003 and became tournament legal on 6 June. The May slip authorizes immediate firing of one eligible weapon at a battle’s initiation. The June revised slip adds “once” to that immediate firing. The August and February supplements print the full wording under Clarification. Both 2003 slips allow that weapon to fire again later in the same battle. The remaster keeps that immediate firing and later opportunity. [https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualCards5.pdf#page=3 Players Committee revised slip p. 3]. [https://web.archive.org/web/20030809111550id_/http://swccgpc.com:80/virtualcards.htm Players Committee dated download index]. [https://web.archive.org/web/20040206210427id_/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Resources/rulessheet08252003.pdf#page=1 25 August 2003 exact clarification]. [https://web.archive.org/web/20040707195107id_/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Resources/rulessheet020904.pdf#page=1 9 February 2004 exact clarification].
